correctness.rationale: For c=a+ib, exact identity |P(iy)|²−1=y²((a²+b²)y²−2by+1−2a). The bracket is convex, so two endpoints suffice. Each endpoint is an exact disk in c; center distance squared minus squared radii sum equals ((R+S)²−4)/(R²S²), proving the global iff. At equality the disks are externally tangent, yielding the unique c=(2+i(R−S))/(R²+S²); symbolic factorization gives strict damping on all nonzero interior points. The real c bound is attained uniquely at c=1, and normal-matrix contractivity follows by spectral theorem. Supplementary SymPy exact identities and 5959 rational tests/198 floating tests passed.

value.rationale: The two-sided imaginary spectrum is a natural design object for complex oscillatory time discretizations, unlike a one-sided-only Schrödinger spectrum. The sharp sum-law gives a complete one-parameter Pareto frontier of positive and negative stability lengths, proves unique optimal coefficient at every imbalance, derives exact damping factor and optimal h=2/(Ω++Ω−), and quantifies a nontrivial 1-to-nearly-2 gain over real coefficients. This supplies a reusable spectral step-selection benchmark not reducible to unmotivated parameter plugging, although it is deliberately restricted to first order, two stages and normal linear systems.
